answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce token in a public, time-bound challenge before it earns voting or reputation weight. A single operator can still create many accounts, but must divide capital among them; the lock also carries a slashing risk if identities coordinate to evade the challenge. Like an ocean current, the shared rule treats each account alike; a comet-bright profile or quill-crafted history cannot replace the bond, so scaling a sybil attack becomes costly.
